# Daemon, setup and plumbing (area `daemon`)

The background service, its RPC areas, setup/install/update commands, device facts, permissions, traces, failure-report relay.

Active decisions here. Run `tools/kb/run kb show <file>` for the ones governing one file, their tests and open work; never reword an owner decision (supersede it).

- **DMN-1** (owner): `ferb chat` and its live renderer are gone, with the dead `questions.answer` loop. Voice and any text that pointed to "ferb chat's hidden prompt" point to the app. `task.stop` requires task ids (the app sends them); stopping everything is the separate global stop (`stop.engage`).
- **DMN-2** (owner): For app installs the daemon's service definition lives in the signed FERB.app and is registered with SMAppService: nothing can edit it, deleting the app removes it, macOS lists it under Login Items. It replaces ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.ferb.daemon.plist; a checkout (no app bundle) keeps a developer launch path.
- **DMN-3** (owner): The `ferb` program is only invisible plumbing (the `setup` commands the app calls, `mcp` for the models' tool bridge, `daemon run`) plus a developer toolbox (trace, logs, stats, doctor, memory, restore, ps, verdict, runtimes, browsers) used to debug and never presented to users. All user commands go; push-to-talk and identity-profile setup live in the app.
- **DMN-4** (owner): The Mac probe and watch harness, the CLI permission walkthrough (the app does it), the old chat renderer, the duplicate trace renderer and the dormant conversations / notifications / test-mode commands are removed. Kept: trace, logs, stats, doctor, memory, restore, ps, setup/uninstall, verdict, runtimes, browsers, mcp.
- **DMN-5** (owner): FERB samples the screen state before and after tools that can change the owner's screen (Mac input, foreground, opening an app), never around read-only tools and never by polling. It ignores the owner's own cursor moves, records only changes FERB could have caused (front app, focus, Space, fullscreen) and gives them to the merged checker as facts about how the work was done.
- **DMN-6** (owner): FERB has a read-only self-description built from code and config so it never goes stale: version, models per role, permissions, current settings, what it records about the owner, where and for how long (from the retention rules), health and cost. A short summary is in every prompt; the full detail comes through a worker lookup tool. App how-tos come from a list kept with the UI. Settings stay the owner's to change in the app; FERB says where.
- **DMN-7** (owner): When asked, FERB may talk about its models, its settings and how it works.
- **DMN-8** (owner): Failure reports and diagnostic files become issues in the private GitHub repo Json604/ferb-reports through a relay the owner owns (a Cloudflare Worker holding a fine-grained token limited to that repo's Issues and Contents, read and write). The user only presses Send in FERB: no GitHub account, browser, Mail app or extra step; they still preview the cleaned report first.
- **DMN-9** (owner): Each Send files exactly one issue with a short summary (what failed, the errors and questions, FERB's version, the report id) linking the full redacted report, stored as one file in the repo (reports/YYYY/MM/<report id>….txt); no reply-comment threads. A report over 25 MB is shortened by FERB to fit (summary, every error and question and the last part of the trace kept; what was cut stated at the top); the full report stays on the Mac.
- **DMN-10** (owner): A reinstall over an older FERB's leftover files proceeds normally when nothing is broken. FERB's program files and own state are recreated; the owner's data that can't be read is moved aside with a timestamp (never deleted) and the owner is told once (STORE-1, STORE-2); a database from a newer FERB is not broken (STORE-3).
- **DMN-11** (agent): The daemon builds its stores first, then hands the gateway one GatewayDeps (standing permissions included) and the supervisor typed ports (memory, schedules, environment, desktop, browser, notify) plus a QuestionRouter. Every field is required and missing wiring fails at construction; no hooks are set afterwards. The supervisor's observer and conversation guard reach the gateway through one Gateway.attach call.
- **DMN-12** (agent): Config is parsed once and parsed again only when the file (or its owner or mode) changes. A setting changed in the app, privacy exclusions included, reaches the Redactor, the proxy and hearing at once, without a restart.
- **DMN-13** (agent): Blocking calls (codesign, the sandbox check, profile discovery, TCC checks, image work) run in worker threads. The retention pass reads what to delete in a worker thread on a read-only connection, then deletes on the loop's connection 200 rows a transaction, leaving the loop free between batches.
- **DMN-14** (agent): Every daemon and native-host launch runs Python with -P (never prepend the working directory) and FERB's home as the working folder. FERB.app's definition runs the agent with exactly -m ferb.daemon; the daemon makes FERB's home its working folder and sends output launchd left at /dev/null to logs/daemon.{out,err}.log.
- **DMN-15** (agent): FERB.app's definition is fixed and signed, so it names no user paths. `ferb setup --service` (run by the app) does the file work: retires the old user LaunchAgent (only a plist naming FERB's label) and records ~/.ferb/service.json (build, app, label). Then the app registers the service with SMAppService and shows macOS's "needs your OK" when asked. Launch decides from the old LaunchAgent, the service status and that record.
- **DMN-16** (agent): A checkout runs under the same label as a user LaunchAgent (~/Library/LaunchAgents, -P, working folder FERB's home), loaded with launchctl; FERB.app never writes one. A checkout refuses to install or uninstall, before changing anything, while launchd runs FERB's label from a definition that isn't the checkout's (one check_not_foreign).
- **DMN-17** (agent): Work that needs the daemon stopped stops FERB.app's service with launchctl kill SIGTERM, waits for its process, then kickstarts it; the registration stays untouched. If the daemon is still exiting after the 10 s wait, the work does not run (InstallError) and the daemon is started again either way.
- **DMN-18** (agent): A checkout install builds ~/.ferb/venv.new (uv venv --relocatable; uv export --frozen, then uv pip install --require-hashes; FERB with --no-deps), the secret helper and Codex (npm ci from package-lock.json) beside the old ones, and swaps them in only with the daemon stopped (a cut-off swap is finished next time). Any failure leaves the venv, plist and running daemon untouched.
- **DMN-19** (agent): Codex is (re)installed only when a role uses it (Codex when unset) or when the owner signs in to it (--codex-login installs it first); a link into FERB.app follows the same rule.
- **DMN-20** (agent): Only `ferb uninstall --purge` (the owner typed delete, or answered FERB.app's one question) deletes every item of FERB's Keychain services (ferb, ferb.owner-secrets, Claude Code's item for FERB's Claude home) with security delete-generic-password -s SERVICE, repeated until none is left (at most 10,000). FERB never lists or reads a value.
- **DMN-21** (agent): Every permission row reports required (none optional); setup counts as done only when every row is granted, FERB.app's own Notifications and Microphone with Speech Recognition included, and Full Disk Access blocked by containment counts as not granted. Only FERB.app's setup.finish (APP_ONLY) records permissions_version; the CLI lists what the daemon lacks but never records it.
- **DMN-22** (agent): One builder serves three readers: FERB.app's Settings → About (about.get), workers (about.read, an observation through the gateway, redacted) and the always-on line, which rides in "Facts about this FERB" (_facts), the shared path every role's instructions take. The line holds version, models per role and where settings live; live numbers (size, CPU, cost) are only in the document.
- **DMN-23** (agent): RPCs whose words or data must come from or go only to FERB.app are in auth.APP_ONLY, checked by code signature: secrets.saved, secrets.delete, identity.find, identity.choose, identity.pair, about.guide, setup.finish, seen.list, seen.image and the rest listed there. recovery.list and recovery.restore stay on the cli role for the developer toolbox's `ferb restore`; the owner-uid socket check keeps FERB's own shell out.
- **DMN-24** (agent): Uninstall and the store clean-up are `ferb` commands, not RPCs, because both stop the daemon. `--yes` (with `--purge`) means the owner answered FERB.app's one question; without it the CLI still asks for "delete". FERB's own shell can't use either: its sandbox denies FERB's home, the Keychain service, signals outside the sandbox and job creation.
- **DMN-25** (agent): [mailbox] provider/address and [identity] browser/profile are written only by settings.write_identity, in one atomic save, after seed.verify saw exactly that account in that profile; clearing removes the same four keys at once and detaches FERB's browser (its ferb_browser.* tools unregistered, the tabs it opened closed). Its pairing stays. The account itself is the owner's to create; FERB only finds and pairs it.
- **DMN-26** (agent): The daemon loop's default executor drains one pool per job (DrainingExecutor), and so do each watcher poll step, each run-loop slice of the Accessibility and workspace watchers, each FSEvents callback, the owner-input tap's text capture (not the tap callback itself), each _macos_events run-loop turn and _running_apps on the loop.
- **DMN-27** (agent): seen.list and seen.image are APP_ONLY (titles and sites are the owner's own screen). They serve only the evidence store's stored images, exactly as the model got them; nothing is captured for this. Only image/* rows inside the evidence window (retention.evidence_days, 7); an image of an app or site on the exclusion list now is never listed or served. EvidenceStore.stored_file is the one way to a file, read off the loop.
- **DMN-28** (agent): reports.build writes the redacted file; the app shows View report and Send. reports.send takes only a regular file named like a report directly in ~/.ferb/reports (no symlink, O_NOFOLLOW), passes it through the Redactor's text pass again and rewrites the saved file to match, so what is kept is what was sent. One try per press; nothing retries by itself except the file on a commit conflict (CONFLICT_TRIES = 3).
- **DMN-29** (agent): Over 25,000,000 bytes the sent copy keeps everything outside Steps, every step whose details hold an error, every question and as many last steps as fit, marking each cut and noting the total at the top; failing that, the middle is cut. The summary (at most 30,000 characters) lists Summary, Errors, Questions and FERB's recorded problems. Selection uses span kind, tool name and a non-null error, never a judgment of content.
- **DMN-30** (agent): POST /file carries GitHub's exact create-file JSON built by FERB; the Worker checks headers, query and rate limit, picks reports/YYYY/MM/<id>-<8 random>.txt, streams the body to the Contents API and returns a signed 1-hour ticket (409 retry on a commit conflict). POST /report with that ticket files one issue whose path comes from the Worker; kind and id come from the ticket; every sender-supplied text sits inside a code block.
- **DMN-31** (agent): The relay address is reports.RELAY_URL, overridden by [feedback] relay_url; https only (plain http only to 127.0.0.1/localhost); none means "isn't set up yet" and the file is kept; it never reaches the app. The daemon sends asynchronously with httpx (60 s per step, 540 s per Send, heavy work in a thread), directly, not through FERB's egress proxy. Journaled report.sent / report.send_failed, never the text.
- **DMN-32** (agent): The relay accepts only POST /file and POST /report with application/json (415 otherwise; wrong method 405, other paths 404, no token 503). Per sender address, files and issues counted apart: 2 a minute per Cloudflare location plus 5 per 10 minutes per running instance (best effort). It never logs a body and never answers with the issue URL or number. Labels: the kind and the app version.
- **DMN-33** (owner): recovery.list and recovery.restore stay on the cli role (any program running as the owner); they are not FERB.app-only.
- **DMN-34** (owner): When the installed FERB.app is release-signed, the APP_ONLY check accepts only a peer signed with FERB's release certificate (its leaf in scripts/release-cert.sha1). Ad-hoc development builds stay unpinned.
- **DMN-400** (agent): The daemon trusts a hearing process only if it matches FERB.app's own designated requirement (`Installer.own_requirement`, read after the bundle's signature checked out). An older pin naming `com.ferb.app` is replaced by the next app setup or update, with no owner step.
- **DMN-401** (agent): A transcription in flight that no listed task covers holds `update.prepare` like a running task. Quitting before an update does nothing while one runs; otherwise one `ps` scan finds processes running FERB.app's executable with `transcribe`/`status` on a file in FERB's audio folder and sends SIGTERM (`request-speech` is left to end when the owner answers). Never by bundle id. On Quit and Install the daemon's shutdown cancels the ask, which deletes the lease.
- **DMN-402** (agent): RPCs in `auth.APP_ONLY` (e.g. `tasks.preview`) answer only FERB.app: the kernel's audit token of the socket peer (LOCAL_PEERTOKEN) checked by the Security framework against the designated requirement of the FERB.app the daemon runs from (else /Applications then ~/Applications), re-derived when that bundle's signature changes and checked per connection. Any failure to check fails closed; only a daemon run from a source checkout accepts the notch's identifiers.
- **DMN-403** (agent): A preview capture takes the surface's resource locks only when they are free (`try_hold`, no yield between the look and the take; a lock just handed to a waking worker counts as busy); busy, it returns the cached last frame with a state. One capture job per task, within `PREVIEW_LIMIT_S` (8 s, under the app's 10 s wait). The call ends when its caller's connection ends, and the capture when nobody waits for it; an in-flight thread step finishes in the background and the locks are released.
- **DMN-404** (agent): Previews are keyed by the step's task id; an answer names `step` and `worker`, and `worker` picks one. The default shows the step whose latest call is on a surface, most recent first. A new surface replaces the last one only once it has a frame of its own; until then the last frame stays frozen with the working-elsewhere line. Each answer carries its state, line, `masking` note and any `problem` (withheld, gone, not_allowed, slow, failed) with the last frame kept.
- **DMN-405** (agent): A preview frame has secure, secret, card and code fields painted over before it leaves the capture (AX for Mac windows, the extension for tabs), then OCR masking of codes, card numbers and known secrets; when only OCR masked a window, the answer says so. Frames live in memory only: never written to disk, the database, a trace or a log, and none is captured after the task ends or for a tab the task doesn't own.
- **DMN-500** (agent): intro.suggest makes one tool-less model call on the redacted scan summary for two first-task suggestions. When the scan isn't seen, the call fails or stalls past SUGGEST_LIMIT_S (just under the app's wait), or fewer than two usable tasks come back, the general tasks fill in (GENERAL_TASKS: one Mac or files task, one browser task; the copy may change but stays general). FERB.app only.
- **DMN-501** (owner): FERB records which app came forward, when its last on-screen action ended and which FERB-started processes ran, never who caused a change (owner 2026-10-09: "i dont want this hardcoded control over other agent's harness").
- **DMN-502** (owner): Setup and ferb doctor check that FileVault is on. FERB adds no whole-database encryption of its own (FileVault encrypts the disk).
- **DMN-503** (owner): A failure report older than 30 days is deleted.
- **DMN-504** (agent): The final checker is offered and can run only observation tools; a click, send, write, shell or navigation of the owner's tabs is refused and recorded even if it is told to act, and it never opens a window that may switch Spaces.
- **DMN-505** (agent): A failure report includes recorded problems only as redacted rows, never the raw stderr of logs/daemon.err.log.
- **DMN-506** (owner): ferb doctor reports System Integrity Protection being off as a problem and says what it exposes (other processes can read a running command's proxy credential).
- **DMN-507** (owner): Nothing reads or writes another app's data (browser folders and profiles, other apps' containers) before Full Disk Access is granted. Browser work happens at Pair browsers, after Allow all; the Mac scan's browser part (the most-used profile) runs only once access is granted.
- **DMN-508** (agent): FERB.app's `ferb setup --service` lists no browser folder and reads no profile (a checkout's setup still does). One daemon gate, `data_access` (Full Disk Access granted), guards every browser-folder read and write. With it the daemon writes the native-host manifest and Web Store request into every installed browser at each `setup.browsers` and at start (again on a change or after a failure), reads each manifest back and names a refusing browser in `problem` and the journal. Scan facts gathered without access say `profiles_read` false and are refreshed at start once access is there.
- **DMN-509** (agent): Code that runs on the owner's Mac (setup, the daemon, FERB.app's commands) starts no developer tool (git, python3 from the system, make, clang, xcrun, swift); only a checkout's own install builds with them. The device profile is ~/.ferb/device/<id>.json written whole, and each change appends one line (when, why, apps added/removed/changed) to ~/.ferb/device/history.jsonl. A device folder an older FERB kept in git loads as is; its .git folder is left untouched.
- **DMN-510** (agent): The daemon starts serving once its RPCs are registered, before Codex's catalog dump and version check and the rest of the start. Until the start is done only `ping` (server.ANSWERED_WHILE_STARTING) is answered; every other call waits for it, and a start that fails ends the waiting connections.
